parallelSafe: The two files are independent, so one HangarUI worktree and one Renderer worktree can run in parallel (they share no imports except ShipClient.ts importing HangarUI, and Game.ts importing both, and neither cut changes public APIs). Inside each file, cuts are sequential. Within HangarUI: hangarHelpers.ts first, then hangarCanvas and hangarPanels (these two touch disjoint line ranges and can go in separate worktrees, but both edit the import block and class shell, so merge one after the other and rebase). hangarDesigns and wires go last. Within Renderer: worldFx and entityLayer touch disjoint ranges and can run in parallel with a trivial import-line merge; worldBackdrop/overlays go after worldFx. Do each file as one agent in one worktree where possible, since the line ranges drift as soon as another cut lands. Wait for a quiet window: no other agent may be editing the same file, and per the audit (section 7) do not start while four agents are editing the god-files.
verification: Behaviour-preserving, so verify by compile, tests and before/after images. (1) npx tsc --noEmit for client and the root build, plus a check that no file imports a cycle (npx madge --circular client/src/rendering client/src/ships, or a short grep script). (2) npx vitest run client/src/rendering client/src/assets client/src/ships client/src/ui/componentGuide.test.ts (cameraView, wireEdit, modelCards, partPresentation, AsteroidLook, assetCache). There is no HangarUI or Renderer unit test, so add small tests for the extracted pure parts (hangarHelpers, and the FxLayer particle-lifetime and cap logic if made pure). (3) Panels: take before/after shots with scripts/boss-shots/shoot.mjs in the live game (one headless browser, closed afterwards, per docs/panels/README.md). Capture the hangar with power overlay, circuits overlay, wires tool, palette each category, summary and load test; capture the world with a firefight (hit sparks, explosion, tractor beam, damage numbers, death screen), a warp, a station and the minimap; images must be pixel-identical or visually identical at the same framing. (4) Measure frame cost before and after with node scripts/profile/loadTime.mjs and the in-game CPU ms per frame (guide reports 0.4-1.2 ms); the number must not rise. (5) Confirm exports: Game.ts and the 6 other Renderer importers and ShipClient.ts compile with no edit. (6) Diff check: a script that confirms the moved functions' bodies are textually identical apart from this. substitutions.
suggestedModel: Sonnet for the mechanical moves (hangarHelpers, hangarDesigns/wires, rendererOverlays, worldBackdrop) since they are cut-and-paste with import fixing. Opus for hangarCanvas, hangarPanels, entityLayer and worldFx: they must design the narrow context interfaces, spot hidden shared-state mutations through this, and keep the per-frame path allocation-free. tokenEstimate: About 600-800k tokens in all. HangarUI: helpers about 60k, canvas about 120k, panels about 180k, designs/wires about 60k. Renderer: worldFx about 120k, entityLayer about 90k, backdrop/overlays about 100k. Verification and screenshot runs about 80k. Roughly 1-2 days of agent wall time, one agent per file. This is more than the guide-writing pass (1.1M total) per line moved, because agents must read the slice they move plus its callers.
hazards: Worth doing now or later: HangarUI is worth splitting now, but only the safe pair (hangarHelpers.ts and hangarCanvas/Power) first. It is the hot file: the last two commits (5896116 +155/-18, 1f17f26 +63/-1) were both power and circuit overlay and palette work, and the next planned work (more power types, circuits, parts) lands in the canvas, the panels and the stats. It has no tests, so keeping logic in modules is also the guide's own advice. Renderer is stable: of its 7 commits, only the first (3a57da7) was large, then bceb4ed removed 199 lines, and the rest are 1-30 line tweaks. The split is lower value, and the audit itself says 'Renderer.ts: do last' and that it needs a Layer interface that does not exist yet. Defer the Renderer split until P1/P4 on GameServer and ShipBridge are done, or do only the FxLayer extraction (worldFx.ts), which is the one piece agents add to (new world effects go through showEffect).

Hot parts of Renderer: showEffect and the create*Effect methods (1339-1569, new world effects), setQuality (1691, new quality knobs), collectLights, and the entity graphics for new entity types (979). Stable parts: camera/pan (652-745), coordinate transforms (1627-1690), renderBackground (746-821), death screen, minimap, bloom, onResize, lighting set-up. Hot parts of HangarUI: drawPower/drawCircuits (1925-2104), powerHtml/summaryHtml/renderStats (1461-1659), the palette (908-1229, categoryOf/filterCat, partListsHtml), placementProblem/candidateMounting (451-489). Stable: constructor DOM set-up, open/close/keys, saved designs (677-764), load list (603-676), tooltips, module helpers.

Prediction drift: neither file runs the shared flight step, but Renderer reads predicted/interpolated positions (the local ship pose, tagScale, orbitFocus, firePoseOf, predictShot, barrelTip, onMuzzle at 1644-1663). Moving these into layers must not change which position (predicted vs server) each reads, nor the call order of updateCamera and renderEntities within a frame, or the camera will lag the ship by one frame and look like a desync. Keep the order in update(): camera, background, entities, effects. Keep predictShot, barrelTip and firePoseOf setters on the Renderer facade and pass the references into WeaponFx and FxLayer.

Circular imports: layer files must take what they need by constructor or ctx argument, never import Renderer. Use import type only for the Renderer type. In HangarUI the new files must not import HangarUI; hangarHelpers is a leaf, hangarCanvas and hangarPanels import helpers plus common/ships and wireEdit/partTip/modelCards/shipSummary only. ShipClient.ts imports HangarUI (type or value), so keep HangarDeps and the class exported from the original path (make the original file re-export). Run a cycle check as part of verification.

Concurrent-edit collisions: the line ranges in the guides drift, so each agent must re-grep method names and not trust the numbers. Another agent adding a weapon, part or effect during the split will edit the class being cut (showEffect, partListsHtml, drawPower) and the merge will be a conflict in code that has moved. Rule: announce a freeze on the target file; if a feature must land first, land it, then cut. Keep a thin delegating facade (same public methods on Renderer, same public API on HangarUI) so unrelated files (Game.ts, ShipClient.ts, sandbox.ts) never change. After the split update docs/areas/render-world.md and hangar-ui.md section ranges and their how-to-extend line numbers (guide items cite Renderer.ts:1691, 1339, HangarUI 451, 478, 1529, 2122, 2189), and the router in DEVELOPMENT.md and CONTEXT.md files, or the area guides will point at wrong places. The panels index and PROTOCOL files are not touched.

Perf in the per-tick path: Renderer.update runs every frame at 0.4-1.2 ms CPU; the guide's rules are that effects are pooled sprites, Graphics are not cleared when idle (clearIfDrawn), asteroids are placed once per tick, hostile health bars are redrawn only on change and the minimap is throttled to 20 Hz. A split that adds per-frame object allocation (a fresh ctx object, array spread, bound closures, optional-chaining wrappers in renderEntities or updateEffects) can raise GC. Construct the context objects once and mutate them, keep hot arrays as class fields, and compare ms/frame and heap (about 24 MB steady) before and after. Method calls through an extra class are cheap, but a getter that rebuilds an object per call is not.

Hidden shared state: Renderer has about 150 private fields (177-332) used across methods (entity maps, particles array, flashes, tractor beams, camera state, SystemVisuals). Extracting a layer requires moving the right fields with it; any field used by two layers (flashes feed collectLights; effectContainer is used by FX and the weapon FX; zoom/pose is used by almost everything) must be passed through a small shared interface, not duplicated. HangarUI has the same problem: sel, view, overlays, bp, geoms, derived and the 25 this.ctx uses shared by draw and panels. Design the shared-state interface first, and do not invent a second copy that can go stale (for example a cached bp).

HangarUI-specific: designSig must keep covering every power-affecting blueprint field or the load-test result goes stale; HTML strings must keep going through esc(); tooltip z-index 2100 (PART_TIP_CSS); the keys must stay live through InputManager.raw; bindBuildButtons attaches DOM listeners on every buildHtml, so moving it must not double-bind or leak listeners; the hangar rederives on every edit and refresh must stay cheap (do not add work to refresh while moving code). The server is authoritative, so no rules change.

Renderer-specific: Pixi does not inherit blendMode from a render group onto children (SpritePool and WeaponFx put it on each sprite), and Bloom replays registered containers as render groups, so changing which container a layer is parented to or the order containers are created changes draw order and bloom. Container creation order (177-332 / constructor 333-402) must be preserved exactly. Legacy renderers and sandbox.ts import some pieces; check client/src/sandbox.ts does not reach into Renderer internals (it bundles legacy only, per the guide). Shader warm-up (gameShaders.ts) lists programs and is unaffected unless the star/planet creation moves.

Test gap: neither file has a unit test, so a mistaken move (wrong this-binding, lost event listener, missed field init) will only show in the game. Mitigate with TypeScript strict mode, a mechanical diff check of moved bodies, and screenshots before/after; do not rely on vitest alone. Pure extractions (hangarHelpers, hangarDesigns' key logic, particle-lifetime logic) should get tests as part of the cut.

Order against the other audit work: audit section 5 puts the GameServer/ShipBridge/Game.ts cuts (step 3) and the part registry (step 4) first, and says Renderer 'last'. Registry work (P1) will add hooks to HangarUI palette and tooltips and to Renderer entity graphics/effects, so splitting these two files after P1 means the registry lands in smaller files, but doing HangarUI canvas/helpers now does not conflict with P1 because P1 mostly touches partTip/modelCards/shipSummary, not draw code. Uncommitted work: the git status is clean now, which is the best moment for a one-agent-per-file cut.
